description: Over a six-week period in October to early December, Médecins Sans Frontières documented 1,267 people deported into Reynosa after dark, 588 of them after 8pm.
energy_note: Twelve hundred people, released into the dark.

aspect: The handover itself creates the exposure
description: After release from detention, people are processed by CBP at the international bridge, received by Mexican authorities, then moved to a returnee processing centre - a sequence that can take over three hours, leaving them visible and stationary late at night.
energy_note: Three hours standing in the open, visibly newly deported.

description: MSF's head of mission for Mexico and Central America described 'dumping people in dangerous cities which they don't know after dark' as making an already traumatic process needlessly more damaging.
energy_note: The word the aid agency used was dumping.

aspect: EXAMPLE - one in five arrive in the night hours
description: A University of Arizona survey found one in five Mexicans deported from the US reported being repatriated between 10pm and 5am, when services are closed.
energy_note: Arriving at the hour when nothing is open.

aspect: Tamaulipas is not an incidental destination
description: State Department reporting recorded Tamaulipas as having the highest kidnapping rate of any Mexican state, with Mexico's national public security system recording 887 kidnapping cases there in eight months of 2013. Reynosa's homicide rate has risen with conflict between criminal groups.
energy_note: Delivered to the state with the most kidnappings.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the shelter that locks people in
description: Reynosa became dangerous enough that, rather than deportees being locked out of a shelter during the day as is usual, they were locked in.
energy_note: The shelter locks the door from the outside, to protect them.

aspect: The shelter is full and the bus station is where you sleep
description: Capacity in border-city shelters is finite and arrivals are not scheduled to match it, so the overflow sleeps in public - visible, stationary and newly deported.
energy_note: Sleeping where everyone can see he has just arrived.

aspect: And he will try again within the week
description: For a man with citizen children in Illinois, the deportation is an obstacle rather than an ending, which is why DEP-002 records that most decline the ride south.
energy_note: Back at the line on Thursday.
